absent: Partitioning field positions, widths, enable bit encoding, and system register numbers.
Storage definitions and reset values for global default, per processor default, and current partitioning images.
Virtual processor register semantics and vendor call identifier bit layout.
Absolute page size and resulting numeric granule counts and tag storage sizes.
Complete cache maintenance identifier layout and behavior on unusual block sizes.
Capability queries, override controls, and fault status validation effects.
Numeric page flag values and page and folio descriptor layouts.
Full barrier and conditional wait primitives and their ordering guarantees.
User control field layout and fault mode encodings.

findings.text: The partitioning layer offers routines to build a register image from data and instruction partition selectors together with data and instruction grouping selectors, to install a default image for a named processor, and to publish or fetch the image associated with a thread control block.

Context handling is inert when the feature gate is off and also when the incoming image already matches the resident image. A task image equal to the global default is replaced by the calling processor default before comparison, and an alternate build provides an empty routine.

When an update is required, privileged partitioning state is refreshed before an ordering barrier and before unprivileged state, with an additional streaming extension register refreshed only on capable systems. Unprivileged synchronization completion is deferred until return to unprivileged execution.
Hypervisor register access is layered so that generic setters and getters forward to virtual processor register primitives, and the non nested variants forward to the generic ones.
The vendor hypervisor invocation uses standard call conventions with sixty four bit secure monitor semantics under the vendor hypervisor owner and function number one.

Memory tagging uses sixteen byte granules with fifty six bit tag position and four bit tag width. Derived facts include granule count per page, tag storage per page, an alignment mask, a tag field mask, and an assembler prefix enabling the tagging extension.
A predicate reports whether asynchronous or asymmetric tagging is in use through a runtime patchable branch in one build and reports false unconditionally in the other build.
Tag check override helpers for asynchronous mode conditionally suppress or restore checking only when the asynchronous predicate holds. The alternate build provides empty helpers.
Pointer tags for sanitizer use fix the high nibble while carrying address high bits in the low nibble. The fallback build returns all bits set.

Memory tag retrieval reads the allocation tag of the referenced granule and then decodes it as a pointer tag, while random tag creation produces an unpredictable tag through hardware generation. Fallback builds return all bits set.
Low level primitives provide single granule tag store with pointer advance by one granule, zeroing store with advance, and block oriented cache maintenance with and without zeroing.

Range tagging guarantees complete coverage while using block maintenance only for sufficiently large aligned interiors where hardware permits, using single granule stores elsewhere, and preserves the caller initialization choice by selecting zeroing or non zeroing forms consistently.

When hardware tagging support is unavailable, range tagging and kernel mode enablement for synchronous and asynchronous and asymmetric modes do nothing, while store only enablement reports an invalid argument failure.

Publishing a page as tagged is ordered after prior tag writes with a write barrier, and observing a tagged page is ordered before subsequent tag reads with a read barrier. Flag identities reuse architecture specific page flag slots.

Acquisition for page tagging uses an atomic test and set on a dedicated lock flag. Success grants initialization rights. Failure waits with acquire semantics until the tagged flag appears and then reports no work.

A regular page moves from untagged to under initialization to tagged. Only the acquirer performs initialization and publication. Concurrent callers observe the transition and proceed without initializing.

Without tagging support the page helpers report untagged and decline acquisition, address and copy and zeroing helpers do nothing, thread and suspend helpers do nothing, control accessors report success with zero, and tag copy through tracing reports an input output failure.

Huge page folio tagging mirrors the regular page discipline with publication and observation barriers plus lock flag acquisition and waiting, while the unsupported build does nothing and reports untagged and declines acquisition.

Exception entry restores tag checking only when the processor supports tagging and either sanitizer hardware tags are active or the incoming thread requests synchronous or asymmetric checking in its saved control state.

Fault status validation on entry and exit is active only when sanitizer hardware tags are enabled and asynchronous handling is in use. Exit adds data and instruction synchronization before validation, and alternate builds provide empty entry and exit and low level validation helpers.
The signed sixty four bit intrinsic type is long long and the unsigned is unsigned long long, and neon presence equals floating SIMD support.
The mediated backtrace trigger and activity query report inactivity, and the processor stop helper does nothing in the routed fallback.

User page copying aliases generic page copying, the page table pointer type is a pointer to the page descriptor, movable folio allocation is marked available, high page copy markers are advertised, and default data mapping permissions include task execution with an optional tagging allowance in one build.
The smallest IO port is four thousand ninety six, bus reassignment follows a global reassignment flag, write combining mapping is always permitted, and paravirtual time initialization is empty.

Per processor offset management writes the current offset to the thread register appropriate for the virtualization extension state, and reads it back through hypervisor or kernel variants with the kernel read protected against compiler reordering through a stack reference.

Per processor memory access covers one, two, four, and eight byte widths with single copy read and write semantics and atomic modify operations that select between exclusive load store loops and large system extension instructions at build or boot time.

Current processor accessors disable preemption without tracing around the raw processor pointer operation and then re enable it, with returning forms preserving the observed value across the critical section.
Compatibility write and read barriers delegate to thirty two bit compatibility barrier primitives.
Regular page tagging helpers diagnose huge page misuse while folio helpers diagnose non huge page misuse. Misuse detection is present only in the enabled builds.
Routed headers provide standard inclusion guards that prevent repeated inclusion.
